name: ALGOL 60
note: recursion, call-by-name, and a famously formal syntax
typeSystem: Static; supported recursive procedures and both call-by-name and call-by-value parameter passing. Its report famously used and popularised a formal syntax notation developed by John Backus for the earlier IAL work and adapted by Peter Naur, later called Backus-Naur Form (BNF).
runtime: Compiled ahead-of-time to native machine code by era implementations; the Burroughs B5000 famously co-designed its stack-based hardware architecture specifically to run ALGOL 60 efficiently.

runtimes.name: Native (e.g. Burroughs B5000, GIER ALGOL)
runtimes.role: Multiple independent native-code compilers implemented the ALGOL 60 report; the Burroughs B5000 built stack-oriented hardware support directly around it.

concurrencyModel: N/A (no concurrency constructs in the standard)

codeExample.caption: A counted loop; print is an implementation-specific I/O procedure
codeExample.source:
begin
  integer i;
  for i := 1 step 1 until 10 do
    print(i)
end
